cards.text: Last time, the people of Bethel asked if they should keep weeping and fasting in the fifth month (Zechariah 7:3). God answered through Zechariah, a prophet, by reminding them how their fathers refused to listen (Zechariah 7:11-12). Now the word of the LORD of Hosts comes to Zechariah AGAIN, and friend, I'm leaning in like it's the last ten seconds on the oven timer.

First thing God says: 'I am jealous for Zion with great zeal; I am jealous for her with great fervor.' When I say something twice, it's because nobody heard me, but when God says it twice, friend, you'd better sit DOWN.

cards.question: God says He is jealous for Zion with great zeal. True or false: that means He has given up on her.
God has big feelings about Zion. What does He say He will do there?

answers.text: Scatter His people from it again
Hand it over to a new king

cards.text: And once the LORD dwells there, Jerusalem gets a new name: the City of Truth. Big upgrade, friend, because the best name I ever got in the drawer was 'that thing under the takeout menus.'

cards.question: The LORD will be dwelling there too. So what will the mountain of the LORD of Hosts be called?

cards.text: Then God paints a picture: old men and old women sitting along Jerusalem's streets again, each with a staff in hand because of great age. Friend, I want THAT retirement plan: a bench, a staff, and nowhere to be.

cards.question: Old folks line the streets. And God says the streets of the city will be filled with boys and girls ___ there.

cards.text: Then God asks a question. If this is impossible in the eyes of the remnant of this people in these days, should it also be impossible in His eyes?

cards.question: God asks if what looks impossible to the remnant should be impossible to Him too. What's His point?

answers.text: The promise may not come true

cards.text: Next God says, 'I will save My people from the land of the east and from the land of the west.' East AND west, friend, that's not a pickup, that's a whole ROUTE.

cards.question: After saving His people from the east and the west, God says He will bring them back to dwell in ___.
Once His people are home in Jerusalem, God says they will be His people, and He will be their faithful and righteous God. True or false?

cards.text: Now God speaks to everyone hearing these words from the prophets, the ones who were there when the foundations were laid to rebuild the temple, the house of the LORD of Hosts.

cards.question: What does God tell the people hearing the prophets who were there at the temple's foundations?

answers.text: Let the work rest a while

cards.text: Then God looks back to before those days, when neither man nor beast received wages. Friend, when even the BEASTS aren't getting a paycheck, that's a rough economy.

cards.question: True or false: back then, nobody who came or went was safe from the enemy, because God had turned every man against his neighbor.

cards.text: But now God says He will not treat the remnant of this people as He did in the past. My favorite kind of sentence, friend, is the one that starts with 'but now.'

cards.question: God won't treat the remnant the way He did in the past. So what does He promise them?

answers.text: Their enemies will bring them gold

cards.text: The seed will be prosperous, the vine will yield its fruit, the ground its produce, and the skies their dew. And God gives all of it to the remnant as an inheritance.

cards.question: The house of Judah and the house of Israel have been a curse among the nations. Now God says He will save them, and they will be a ___.

cards.text: Then God says, 'Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong.' That line again, and friend, my hands are a MUSTACHE, so I am doing curls RIGHT NOW.
Then God looks back again. When their fathers provoked Him to anger, He resolved to bring disaster upon them.

cards.question: True or false: once God resolved to bring disaster on their fathers, He relented.
God resolved on disaster back then and didn't back down. So what has He resolved to do now?

answers.text: Do good again to Jerusalem and Judah
Wait and see how Judah behaves
Bring disaster on all the nations

cards.text: And again: 'Do not be afraid.' But this good news comes with a to-do list, friend, like the brand new oven you then have to clean.

cards.question: God says, 'These are the things you must do.' What's the first thing on His list?

answers.text: Build a wall around the city
Offer more sacrifices at the temple

cards.text: They're also to render true and sound judgments in their gates, not plot evil in their hearts against their neighbor, and not love to swear falsely. That should sound familiar, friend, since chapter 7 already says not to plot evil in your hearts against one another (Zechariah 7:10).

cards.question: God tells them not to plot evil against their neighbor or love to swear falsely, for He ___ all these things.

cards.text: Then the word of the LORD of Hosts comes to Zechariah again, and friend, God's about to talk fasts. Remember Bethel's question about weeping and fasting in the fifth month (Zechariah 7:3)?

cards.question: God names the fasts of the fourth, the fifth, the seventh and the tenth months. What does He say those fasts will become?

cards.text: Bethel asked about weeping, and God says those fasts will become cheerful feasts for the house of Judah. Friend, that's like texting 'Should I keep crying?' and getting a PARTY INVITATION back.

cards.question: Because those fasts will turn into joy, God says you are to love both ___ and ___.

cards.text: Then God looks ahead. Peoples will yet come, the residents of many cities.

cards.question: The residents of one city go to another city. What do they say?

answers.text: Let us go and seek the LORD
Let us go and trade in Jerusalem
Let us go and see the new walls

cards.question: One of them says, let us go at once to plead before the LORD. True or false: he sends everybody else but stays home himself.

cards.text: Nope, he says, 'I myself am going.' That's the friend who's already in your driveway with the engine running, honking at YOU.

cards.question: True or false: only a few small nations come to seek the LORD of Hosts in Jerusalem.

cards.text: Many peoples and strong nations come to seek the LORD of Hosts in Jerusalem and to plead before the LORD. Bethel sent Sharezer and Regem-melech and their men to plead before the LORD (Zechariah 7:2), and now it's whole NATIONS, friend.
One last picture. In those days, men from the nations of every tongue will tightly grasp the robe of a Jew.

cards.question: How many men from the nations grab tightly onto the robe of a Jew? ___ men.
These men from the nations hold on tightly to the robe of a Jew. What reason do they give?

answers.text: We have heard that God is with you
We have lost our way in the city
We have come to collect a debt

cards.text: They say, 'Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.' Ten grown men on ONE robe, friend, that's the same grip I've got on the last cookie in the box.

findings.problem: The card says that when 'their fathers' provoked Him, God resolved to bring disaster 'upon them.' Grammatically, 'them' points back to the fathers. But Zechariah 8:14 says the disaster was 'upon you' (the people being addressed) 'when your fathers provoked Me to anger.' The card should keep 'upon you,' for example: 'He resolved to bring disaster on them when their fathers provoked Him.'

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The true-or-false statement says God resolved 'to bring disaster on their fathers.' Zechariah 8:14 says the disaster was 'upon you,' with the fathers' provoking as the occasion. The answer (False) is still right, but the statement misstates who the disaster was on. It should be reworded to match the text, for example: 'once God resolved to bring disaster on them when their fathers provoked Him, He relented.'

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The joke compares the commands to 'the brand new oven you then have to clean.' A brand new oven isn't dirty, so the image doesn't click and needs explaining. The 'good thing that comes with chores' idea falls apart on a new oven. It should be rewritten or cut.

rule.text: It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.

findings.problem: The card cites only Zechariah 8:15, but its line 'this good news comes with a to-do list' tells content from 8:16 ('These are the things you must do'). Either the citation should run 8:15-16, or the card should keep to 8:15 and leave the list to card 14.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card cites only Zechariah 8:18, but 'God's about to talk fasts' tells content from 8:19. Either the citation should run 8:18-19, or the preview of the fasts should be removed.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This two-blank card asks the baker to fill in 'love both ___ and ___' with truth and peace. The two right words can go in either order and mean the same thing. If a baker puts 'peace' in blank 1 and 'truth' in blank 2, the card's blank numbers would mark it wrong, even though the baker could fairly argue it's right.
findings.question: When the two right answers of a two-blank card can be swapped without changing the meaning, should the card be rewritten so only one order works, or should the app accept either order?
